long_biography.plain_text:
Leonid Mikhelson trained as a civil engineer and began his career as a foreman on the Urengoi–Chelyabinsk gas pipeline. His father had led a major Soviet pipeline-construction trust; after rising through the same industry, Mikhelson succeeded him as director. The enterprise became the privatized company NOVA in the early 1990s, providing an operating platform for his later expansion.

In 1994 he took charge of Novafininvest, which accumulated gas-field licences, began production and became NOVATEK in 2003. The company progressively consolidated its producing assets, sold peripheral businesses and built a vertically integrated gas operation. Its development of Yamal LNG then took NOVATEK from Russia's domestic market into large-scale liquefied-natural-gas exports, while Mikhelson remained chairman of the management board.
